note: Rewritten from the original English description by Sands 1959; original in English, the original description of a new species (Amitermes truncatidens sp. n.), type locality Nachingwea, Tanganyika; the original records the worker as indistinguishable from A. evuncifer, so no worker section is given here. In the OCR of the measurements the decimal point has been read as a colon (for example "I:33-1-61" and "O:QI-I-12"), and the ranges have been restored from column position and mean; the head width including the eyes and the pronotum length and width are given as single values only, and are reproduced as single values.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: All castes closely resemble those of A. evuncifer and may eventually prove to be its southern subspecies; as no intermediates are known at present they can be distinguished: the alate fontanelle is a rather wide ellipse and the frons bears two pale, shallow grooves that arise from the fontanellar extension near its ventral end; the soldier head capsule is more inflated above the fontanelle and the mandibular tooth is usually more truncate. The worker cannot be distinguished from A. evuncifer. The soldier is distinguished from the majority of species of the genus, which have spines, by the fore coxa, which has neither spine nor hairs.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Colour: in the female the head and pronotum are mainly sepia brown; the postclypeus and a diffuse pale streak running from the posterior margin of the eye to the back of the head are lighter, yellowish brown; the labrum, antennae, ventral surface of the thorax, femora, tarsi and the middle of the abdominal sternites are pale yellow; the sides of the thorax, the tibiae and the sides of the abdominal sternites are pale yellowish brown; the meso- and metanotal tergites and the abdominal tergites are brown. Posterior margin of the head almost semicircular; fontanelle elliptical, with a narrow pale extension at its anterior end, slightly concave; frons with two pale shallow grooves arising from the fontanellar extension near its ventral end; eyes about as long as the postclypeus; ocelli medium-sized, their distance from the eye slightly less than the width of the ocellus itself; postclypeus about half as long as wide, inflated, anterior margin straight, posterior margin evenly convex; antennae 15-segmented, segments 4 and 5 about equal in length, segment 3 shorter, segment 2 longer than any of these; the third marginal tooth of the left mandible projects beyond the cutting edge between it and the first marginal tooth. Pronotum narrower than the head width including the eyes, anterior margin straight, sides slightly wavy, narrowing posteriorly to a distinctly concave posterior margin. Whole body finely hairy, the hairs of the intersegmental membranes shorter. Male as in the female. Measurements (mm): head width including the eyes 1.07; greatest eye diameter 0.29—0.30; ocellus 0.08—0.09 × 0.12—0.13; ocellus to eye 0.05—0.07; pronotum width 0.89, length 0.50; hind tibia length 1.07—1.13; forewing length 9.50—10.0.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; base of the mandibles yellowish brown, apex chestnut brown; antennae pale yellow, the rest of the body yellowish white, the abdomen coloured by the intestinal contents showing through. Head in dorsal view distinctly longer than wide, sides convex, narrowing slightly anteriorly; posterior margin evenly rounded obtuse or almost round. In side view continuously curved from the fontanelle to the occiput, shallower in front. Mandibles slightly shorter than half the head length, rather stout, strongly hooked; tooth situated a little behind the middle, projecting, erect, truncate to obliquely truncate; inner edge a regular arc from the base of the tooth to the apex. Antennae 14—15-segmented, the proportions of the basal segments variable, segment 2 longer than segments 3, 4 and 5. Head capsule almost hairless except around the fontanelle. Anterior margin of the pronotum entire or slightly concave. Legs almost without hairs or spines except on the tibiae and the ends of the tarsi; fore coxa without spine or hairs. Measurements (mm): head length 1.33—1.61; greatest head width 1.07—1.30; head width at the mandibular base 0.78—0.90; head thickness 0.91—1.12; left mandible length 0.64—0.74; pronotum length 0.32—0.40, width 0.62—0.72; hind tibia length 0.89—1.04.
